title: 数字唯物主义：六只手、机器辅助、怒不可遏

zh: 数字唯物主义：六只手、机器辅助、怒不可遏
en: Digital materialism: six-handed, machine-assisted, furious

zh: 卡罗琳·巴塞特
en: CAROLINE BASSETT

zh: 环顾四周，然后径直切入。
en: Take a look around, then cut through.

zh: 埃莱娜·西苏
en: Hélène Cixous

zh: 新媒介唯物主义是数字媒介研究的一种模式，它宣称自己更接近事物的“真相”，并拒斥其他取径，认为它们是再现性的、只关心图像与扭曲——因而离这种现实或真相更远。这一判断建立在一种预设之上：物质——在此即计算与数字技术的具体材料及其所促成之物——正是事情的核心。与这一研究优先项相一致的是对媒介特定的“怪异物质性”的探索，或以明确的后批判立场思考信息系统的动态。下面没有什么可被揭示，没有超越性之物，也几乎没有在先之物来限定已经到来或将要到来的一切。
en: New media materialism is a mode of digital media studies that declares itself closer to the ‘truth’ of things, and that rejects other approaches as representational, as interested in the image and distortions – and therefore further from this reality or truth. This judgement is founded on a presumption that matter – in this case, the specific materials of computational and digital technologies and what they enable – is at the very heart of the matter. Consonant with this research priority are explorations of the ‘weird materialities’ of the medium-specific, or considerations of the dynamics of information systems that are determinedly post-critical. There is nothing underneath to be revealed, nothing beyond, and almost nothing before to condition what has come, or what will come after.

zh: 这一图景需要被炸开，以服务于作为政治计划的技术女性主义——该计划处理性别不公，这种不公以特定方式被经验，并与其他歧视相交织；或者更系统地说，它被理解为始终已经与其他形式的不平等——尤其是种族、阶级、性与健全主义的不平等——纠缠在一起。
en: This vision needs exploding, in the interests of technological feminism as a political project that addresses gender injustices, experienced in particular ways as they intersect with other discriminations, or, to put this more systematically, understood as always already entangled with other forms of inequality – those of race, class, sexuality, ableism, notably.

zh: 这一图景也需要被探索，因为即便新媒介唯物主义有问题，它也回应了一个时刻，满足了一种需要——一种与新兴技术形式接触和相遇的需求；这种需求不断逼问：我们所说的活动或能动性（人类使用者的、机器的、二者互动的）意味着什么，以及我们所说的赋予生命或活力（animation）、活性、智能、智能生命又意味着什么。
en: This vision also needs exploring, because even if new media materialism is problematic it responds to a moment, addressing a need – a demand for engagement and encounter with emerging forms of technology – that insistently provokes questions not only about what we mean by activity or agency (that of human users, that of machines, their interactions) but also what we mean by animation, liveness, intelligence, intelligent life.

zh: 本文既是对新唯物主义媒介研究的具体考察，也探讨对更广阔局势的一次较早回应——《愤怒》（
），一部合著的专著兼手册，它要求重新思考对数字的物质研究，并坚持这种重新思考可以是批判性的。
它承认新唯物主义对数字媒介研究的吸引力，承认在计算无处不在的当代处境中寻找批判立足点之难，也承认纯粹再现性分析的问题。我们也是唯物主义者，但不是“新唯物主义”意义上的唯物主义者——尤其是因为，我们不承认新唯物主义者所坚持的物质分析与历史唯物主义分析之间的绝对断裂。
en: This essay at once constitutes a specific investigation of new materialist media studies and explores an earlier response to the broader conjuncture,
, a jointly authored monograph/ manual demanding a reconsideration of material studies of the digital and insisting that such a reconsideration can be critical.

It recognizes the appeal of new materialism for digital media studies, the difficulty of finding a critical perch in the contemporary situation of pervasive computation, and problems with purely representational analysis. We are also materialists, although not ‘new materialism’ materialists – not least because we do not recognize the absolute cleavage between material analysis and historically materialist analysis that new materialisms insist upon.

zh: 《愤怒》部分地通过捍卫具身性来回应新唯物主义的主张：把理性理解为具身的、充满激情的、情动的，同时也是逻辑推理的事情。此外，它用具身性（身体的物质性）来思考信息学的物质性。这样做当然使它归于一个在这方面积累了深厚经验的传统：数十年来，女性主义一直在思考技术、认识论与本体论，以及它们与在特定世界秩序中生成的（以不同方式可获得的）可能性之间的关系。而且，它始终关注实例化过程的溢出、杂乱与不完整。正如埃莱娜·西苏1975年对女性所说：“在一次或多或少有意识的计算结束时，她找到的不是她的总和，而是她的差异。”
en: responds to the claims of new materialism, in part, through a defence of embodiment; understanding rationality as embodied, passionate, affective, as well as a matter of logical ratiocination. Moreover it uses embodiment (the materiality of bodies) to think about the materiality of informatics. Doing so, of course, it attaches itself to an expert tradition: feminism has thought about technology, epistemology and ontology and/in relation to the (differently available) possibilities of becoming in a particular world order for decades now. Moreover, it has always been interested in instantiation as excessive and untidy, as incomplete. As Hélène Cixous put it in a 1975 address to women, ‘At the end of a more or less conscious computation, she finds not her sum but her differences.’

zh: 新唯物主义、数字技术与活力论之间关系的政治是什么？这种关系如今为何重要？这样提出问题已经作出一种预设，或已优先选择某种探究模式。这预设了
一种有待探索的关系，而且其意义是政治的。有些人也许更愿意谈论物质、数字与生命，并只通过逗号的“温柔纽结”把它们连接起来。
这或许会产生一种被清除了那些恼人的“额外”主义（例如女性主义）的联系——许多新唯物主义觉得，这些主义会把
搞砸。
en: What are the politics of the relationship between new materialism, digital technologies and vitalism? How does this relationship matter now? To frame the question this way is already to make an assumption, or to prioritize a particular mode of investigation. It is to presume that there

a relationship to be explored, and that its significance is political. Some might prefer to talk of the material, the digital and the vital, and to join them only through the ‘gentle knot’ of the comma.
This might produce a connection purged of those irritating ‘extra’ isms (feminism, for instance) that are felt by many new materialisms to screw
up.

zh: 无论这些联系以何种方式建立（此中关系重大），关于唯物主义、活力与数字或计算的问题，在当前局势中都具有特殊的力量。
一般意义上的数字发展，尤其是人工智能的发展，使一些长期存在的通俗联想甚至等同关系重新凸显：机器的活泼性与有机或人类“生命”本身的思考之间的联想；人类能动性与机器能动性之间的联想；以及媒介自我构成即讯息的能力（麦克卢汉令人难忘地把灯泡理解为一种媒介技术）与常常也被理解为“无内容”的活力论之间的联想。
en: Whichever way these connections are made (much hangs on that) questions concerning materialisms, vitality and the digital or computational arise with a particular force in the current conjuncture.

Digital developments in general and in AI in particular give revived salience to long-standing popular associations or even equivalences: between the liveliness of machines and considerations of organic or human ‘life’ itself; between human and the machinic agency; and between the capacity of the medium to constitute itself as the message (McLuhan memorably understood the light bulb as a medium technology) and vitalism which is often also understood as ‘without content’.

zh: 这些联想如何被理解、其意义可能是什么，是当前数字研究关注的重点，也在公共文化中大量出现——例如作为媒介艺术、在辩论中、在小说中。这一话语作为一个整体，有一个特征：倾向于把实际与预测相融合，把技术未来的想象与现有可能性相融合。这种倾向在更专业的领域中也可见，并可能在那里产生一个起确证作用的（短）回路。例如，社交媒体系统的机器学习系统中所实例化的人工智能算法，也许可以成为在现有计算系统中识别出某种机器活力论的依据。它们的真实存在随后被当作证据，证明关于不久将出现之物、真正的智能或奇点的预测是可靠的；在某些情形中，这采取觉醒的人工生命的形式。我们不妨把这种兴起称为后人类活力论的一种形式。
en: How these associations are understood and what their significance might be preoccupy current digital scholarship, and figure largely in public culture – as media art, in debates, in fiction, for instance. A feature of this discourse taken as a whole is its tendency to fuse the actual with the predicted; imaginaries of technological futures with extant possibilities. This tendency is also in evidence in more specialist registers where it may produce a validatory (short) circuit. The AI algorithms instantiated in machine learning systems in social media systems, for instance, might be grounds for the identification of a kind of machinic vitalism in extant computational systems. Their real existence is then taken as evidence of the reliability of predictions of what will soon arise, true intelligence, or Singularity, in some cases taking the form of awakening artificial life. Let us call this rising a form of post-human vitalism.

zh: 这种发展究竟可能带来善还是恶，在那些最自信地预测其到来的人中间意见分歧。一些奇点论的信奉者对未来生命的新形式明显充满热情；另一些人则宿命般地确信奇点将至，但对它所开启的未来（人类）存在前景更为悲观。
en: Whether such a development would be likely to be for good or ill divides opinions among those who most confidently predict its coming. Some Singularity adherents are markedly enthusiastic about emerging forms of future life; others, fatalistically sure of the advent of Singularity, are more pessimistic about the prospects for future (human) being it opens up.

zh: 对“这一切”，对当前局势的样貌、感受、运作和秩序，另一种回应是愤怒。这正是我想开始的地方。我主张，愤怒是对科技产业的发展优先项与轨迹的一种正当回应——这些优先项与轨迹在多个领域以各种尺度运作；愤怒也是对这些轨迹如何被塑造和决定、对其想象所许诺之物的正当回应。这种愤怒之所以正当，是因为现在和将来都有东西正在被损害、削减、破坏和夺走。一个关键问题是缺乏抱负，缺乏对一切超出市场所赋予价值之物的恰当
，即便这些事物仍被束缚在市场的限制性逻辑之中。
en: A different response to ‘all this’, to the current conjuncture as it looks, as it feels, as it operates and as it orders, is fury. And that is where I want to begin. I assert that fury is a justifiable response to development priorities and trajectories of the tech industries as these operate at various scales across multiple fields; a justifiable response to the ways in which these trajectories are shaped and determined, and to what their imaginaries promise. It is a fury that is justified because of what is being damaged, curtailed, undermined and taken away, now and for the future. A key problem is a lack of ambition, a lack of proper
for all that which exceeds the value it is given by the market, even as it is bound up within its constraining logics.

zh: 此外，我主张，那些把对活力的援引与关于物质性数字物具有先在外在规定性的断言（本体论上的优先性主张）捆绑在一起，并把二者（至少可以肯定，未能将二者与这种许诺分开）附会于数字技术发展即社会进步（更多计算、更多生命）这一未经检验的善的许诺的理论化，正面临产生一种构形的危险：这种构形与上述轨迹捆绑、为其张目，并最终
它们。而不是，比如，开辟各种可能性，以创造和部署智能技术来重新思考可能性的视域和欲望的塑形。我感兴趣的是这种反意识形态构形的意识形态分量，以及它所产生或认可的物质操作与影响，二者相互纠缠。
en: Further, I argue, theorizations that bind up invocations of vitality with assertions of the prior external determination of material digital things (ontological claims for priority) and attach both (or, certainly, fail to detach them) to the promise of digital advance as progress (more computation, more life), as an unexamined good, are in danger of producing a formation bound up with, underscoring and ultimately

these kinds of trajectories. This rather than, for instance, opening up possibilities for creating and deploying intelligent technologies to rethink the horizons of the possible, and the shaping of desire. I am interested in both the ideological heft of this kind of anti-ideological formation and in the material operations and impacts it produces or endorses, these being entangled.

zh: 如果愤怒作为回应显得过于强烈，那么请想想人工智能解决主义在环境危机中的援引；想想把太空探索当作对行星毁灭的回应，或某种通过冷冻保存进入医学上先进的未来时间并重获生命的许诺。在这类解决方案中，总还有另一个空间，总还有另一个时间。或者想想为老年人设计的服务机器人所提供的“友谊套餐”。这里，可替换的机器人被用来交换那个具体的他者——我的朋友，那个人。这种交换的支撑是机器人作为“几乎真的活着”之物的吸引力。这个机器人能成为我的朋友吗？如果你头脑已不如从前，如果你（或为你提供服务的英国国民医疗服务体系，NHS）负担不起“人类”照护，它就能。这里的问题不在于特定任务本身的自动化，也不在于机器不断扩大的能动性，而在于这类（反）社会契约的许诺所包含的替代性造假——以及它对
的依赖。
en: If fury seems too strong as a response, consider the invocation of AI solutionism in relation to environmental crisis; space exploration as a response to planetary devastation, or the promise of renewed life in some cryogenically accessed and medically advanced future time. There’s always another space, always another time, to be had in these kinds of solutions. Or consider the ‘friendship packages’ offered by service robots designed for old people. Fungible robotics are here being offered in exchange for the specific other, my friend, that person. This an exchange underpinned by the appeal of the robot as the almost really alive. Can this robot be my friend? It can if your mind is not what it was and if you (your NHS) cannot afford ‘human’ care. The issue here is not the automation of particular tasks per se, nor the expanding agency of machines, but the substitutional fakery entailed in the promise of this kind of (anti-) social contract – and its reliance on

zh: 这些是残酷的例子。这里援引它们，是为了强调这些问题多么具有政治性，并追问它们
具有政治性——这两者并不完全相同。我希望它们指向这样的方式：生命的许诺、奇点人工智能的完满生命，或在更世俗的领域中被归于特定计算活动形式（机器学习、涌现能动性、机器人人格）的准活力论，能够与计算资本主义及其骇人听闻的不平等的结构相协调，甚至能够
这种结构。人工友谊在字面上就是矛盾。另一种关系是可能的。
en: These are brutal examples. They are invoked here to insist on how political these issues are, and to ask

they are political, which is not quite the same thing. I hope they gesture toward ways in which the promise of life, the full life of Singular AI or, in more mundane spheres, the quasi-vitalism ascribed to particular forms of computational activity (machine learning, emergent agency, robotic personality) can align with, indeed can
to, the structuring of computational capitalism with its obscene inequalities. Artificial friendship is a contradiction in terms. Another relationship is possible.

children: 强制性的（计算）资本主义？

zh: 居于机器人技术核心（或者说头部）的人工智能技术当然属于数字技术，而高端人工智能项目与想象可以被理解为马克·费舍尔令人难忘地称为资本主义现实主义的更大场景中的一个异域（但同样不真实）时刻。
如今，这场景以我们熟悉的方式采取计算形式，包括机器学习、大数据、平台资本主义、无处不在的审查，以及日常生活和工作中的进一步自动化。埃伦·梅克辛斯·伍德曾断言，当市场无法逃避时，资本主义就变得“强制性”了；作为其变体，计算资本主义也可以这样说。
鉴于其全球触及范围和无孔不入的尺度化——从身体内部及远小于身体的尺度，一直到卫星——我们无法像某些人建议的那样简单地
“逃离信息域”。
反计算——有选择地拒斥计算，而非拒斥它所表述的社会关系——并不构成批判性技术政治的基础，因为这两个范畴无法被拆开，或者说拆开就会损害双方。然而，回应圈地处境并非不可能，即便它很可能轻易显得不切实际。毕竟，费舍尔关于资本主义现实主义的要点是：它制造出不可避免性的表象——并把这种表象投射到未来。
en: The AI technologies at the heart of robotics (or at the head of them) are of course digital technologies, and high-end AI projects and imaginaries can be understood as an exotic (but just as unreal) moment in the larger scene of what Mark Fisher memorably called capitalist realism,

now taking on computational form in ways we are familiar with. These ways include machine learning, big data, platform capitalism, pervasive censorship, further automation in the everyday and at work. Ellen Meiksins Wood claimed capitalism became ‘compulsory’ when the market could not be escaped; we might say the same for computational capitalism as a variant of this.
We cannot simply
to ‘escape the infosphere’, as some suggest, given its global reach and its pervasive scaling – from the interior of the body and far below that scale, right up to the satellite.

Anti-computing, a selective rejection of the computational rather than the social relations it articulates, does not provide the basis for a critical technical politics, because the two categories cannot be unbound, or not without damage to each side. Responding to the situation of enclosure, however, is not impossible, even if it may all too easily appear to be unrealistic. Fisher’s point about capitalist realism, after all, was that it produces the appearance of inevitability – and projects that into the future.

zh: 眼下感到愤怒的一个理由是：如果市场的视域能被超越，技术的未来本可以有所不同——例如，关怀可以被重新校准，智能机器与人类之间的互动可以被更有创造性、更有成效、更少还原地探索，或者太空不被视为一个普遍市场。这个论点更难成立，因为计算正以某些方式来到我们面前，正被
我们。
en: One reason to be furious right now is that the technological future could be different if the horizon of the market could be exceeded – so that care, for instance, was recalibrated, or so that interactions between intelligent machines and humans could be more creatively, fruitfully and less reductively explored, or so that space was not viewed as a universal market. This case is the harder to make because of ways in which the computational is coming to us, is being
to us.

zh: 我在此尤其关心的是，关于技术媒介的物质特定性构成当代生命形式（数字存在、人工存在、赛博格存在）之基础的主张，与关于人工生命、人工能动性或活力的主张，如何相互支持。它们由此发挥遮蔽作用，遮蔽能动性形式与行动模式之间、活动与自主性之间的一系列区分或连接。这些区分、它们的维持或消解，都需要被追问。在某些形式中，这种区分的抹除有助于生产一种可感的物质“现实”（一种现实主义），这种现实可能无法被争辩（因为它以本体论为基础），而只能被修改或调制（在此意义上属于“后”批判）。源于本体论的不可争辩之物，应区别于强制性之物：如前所述，后者通过社会关系被安排为一种技术—社会秩序，而这种秩序可以被拒绝。
en: What I am concerned about in particular here are the ways in which claims made about the material specificity of technical media as that which underpins contemporary forms of life (digital being, artificial being, cyborg being) and claims about artificial life or agency or vitality come to support each other. They thereby function to obfuscate a series of distinctions or conjunctions between forms of agency and modes of action, and between activity and autonomy. These distinctions, their maintenance or dissolution, demand interrogation. In some forms their elision contributes to producing a felt material ‘reality’ (a realism) that may not be contested (in that it is based on ontology) but only modified or modulated (and is in this sense ‘post’-critique). The non-contestable, which derives from the ontological, is to be distinguished from the compulsory, as that which, to recap, is ordered through social relations, as a techno-social order, which may be refused.

zh: 这里或许有益的做法是承认：智能机器与人工生命或能动性之间的联系，在这个时代正被重新建立，但它们同样是长期存在的。20世纪初以来电影及其他领域中的机器人诡异感的兴起就表明了这一点。《大都会》（
）会是明显的例子。然而，这些联系以不同方式被处理，并采取新形式——这或许是必要的，因为一方面，这种联系似乎要求被建立（机器的活泼性指向它们的能动性），另一方面，它又包含一种令人不适的结合。试想，计算常常因其
、因其公正、中立、被动、因其能运算数字而受到重视。当程序明显未能按计划运行时，批评往往集中在自动过程未能足够自动或足够人工。人类偏见混入了算法。关切在于人类对新机器“灵魂”的腐蚀：在这一尺度的一端，是由大众媒介训练数据生产出来的“纳粹”机器人；在另一端，是学者们根深蒂固的
倾向。
en: It is perhaps salutary here to recognize that connections between intelligent machines and artificial life or agency, which are being made afresh in this era, are also long-standing. The rise of the robotic uncanny in films and elsewhere from the early twentieth century points to this.

would be the obvious example. However, these connections are worked through in different ways and take new forms – this being necessary perhaps because if, on the one hand, the link seems to demand to be made – the liveliness of machines points to their agency – on the other it entails an uncomfortable joining. Consider that the computational is often valued for being

, for being impartial, neutral, passive, for running the numbers. Criticism when the programme conspicuously fails to run as planned often focuses on the failure of an automatic process to be automatic or artificial enough. Human bias got into the algorithm. The concern is with the human corruption of the ‘soul’ of the new machine: at one end of this scale, mass media training data-producing ‘Nazi’ robots’; on the other, academics’ inveterate tendency to

zh: 或者以奇点话语为例，它是一个更普遍构形的提喻，有助于凸显这里产生的张力。奇点科学当然赞同对可计算之物的偏好，并在评估该领域的物质发展时聚焦于此——例如，如果一台计算机每分钟的计算次数超过某个特定数目，它可能做什么。另一方面，它又容纳一种大规模的、多半未经审视的活力论。因此，在奇点辩论中，活力生命与绝对工具主义的悖论被放大了。在更世俗的语境中，它也在另一个层面运作。我在此指的是类似话语的普遍流通：一种充满张力或悖论性的等同——它说生命被编码，所以算法代码就是生命。我们
我们的虚拟自我吗？这个问题经常被提出。
en: Or take Singularity discourse, a synecdoche for a more general formation, and useful to press home the tensions arising here. Singularity science certainly subscribes to the preference for the calculable and is focused on this when assessing material developments in this field – developments such as what a computer may do if it surpasses a particular number of calculations a minute, let’s say. On the other hand, it entertains a mostly unexamined vitalism operating on a grand scale. The paradox of vital life and absolute instrumentalism is thus writ large in Singularity debates. It is also found operating in a different register in more mundane contexts. I am pointing here to the general circulation of a similar discourse of tensioned or paradoxical equivalence – the one that says life is coded, and so algorithmic code is life.
we our virtual selves? This question is routinely asked.

zh: 一个较少被提出、出现在更具理论性的语域中的问题是：这种等同或混同，究竟是通过一种还原或抽象模式（借助基于系统论的控制论叙述，把机器与人的行动化约为系统性抽象）构成的，还是通过一种新的或复兴的后人类（或反人类）活力论构成的？事实上，这两种取径往往相互逆转。十年前，斯科特·拉什指出，数字媒介系统的兴起带来了一种活力论的复兴，它理解的不是“以生命看待媒介，而是以媒介看待生命”，从而产生了“信息是活的”这类说法。
这并不完全是活力唯物主义，而是数字唯物（主义），它意味着对一种活力物质的描述。拉什认为，这种复兴（他称之为新活力论的兴起——我们或可称之为数字活力论）之所以发生，“是因为内容本身，乃至生命本身，已被卷入金融、信息和媒介的全球流动”。他由此论证，这种活力论形式植根于一种媒介或信息启发法。如果我们接受——
——新媒介的主导内容就是媒介本身，这一说法或许更有说服力。再媒介化理论迷恋旧媒介的形式，接受一种固定而实则偶然的内容/媒介硬性区分，并表现出一种有问题的媒介序列感，因而被过分强调了。
en: A question asked less often, figuring in more theoretical registers, is whether this equivalence or conflation is constituted through a mode of reduction or abstraction (via a cybernetic account based on systems analysis in which machine and human actions are rendered into systemic abstraction) or by way of a new or revived form of post-human (or anti-human) vitalism. The two approaches in fact tend to reverse into each other. A decade ago Scott Lash noted that the rise of digital media systems produced the revival of a form of vitalism that understood not ‘media in terms of life, but life in terms of media’, producing talk of ‘information is alive’.

This is not quite a vital materialism, but digital material(ism) as entailing the description of a vital material. Lash suggested that this revival (the rise of what he terms a neo-vitalism – which we might term a digital vitalism) occurred ‘because content itself and indeed life itself is swept up in the global flows of finance, information and media’. He thus argues that this form of vitalism has its roots in a media or information heuristic. This might be the more persuasive if we accept –

McLuhan – that the dominant content of new media is the medium itself. Remediation theory, with its obsession with the forms of old media, and which accepts as fixed a hard content/medium division that is contingent, and that also exhibits a problematic sense of medium seriality, is overplayed.

zh: 对数字媒介之
的不同理解，如何导致对
与
之间关系的不同刻画？具体而言，各种采取强新唯物主义取径的媒介理论，如何回应来自硅谷的讯息？这讯息在其产品中被表述，在其话语中显而易见：关于进步的讯息，关于更多的讯息——更多技术、更多活动、更多能动性、更多控制、更多

。这一讯息与计算实例化相抵触：对于那些生活在其强制性基础之内的大多数人（对我们所有人而言则以有差异的方式），这些实例化往往产生上述一切的反面。我的回答是：只要这些叙述接受而非质疑某种特定意义上的物质进步的优先性，并因此也预先决定了对活力论（这种活力论是从一种对自身并不好奇的媒介启发法中得到定型的）的回应，它们就没有提供充分的回应。从一种不认同新唯物主义、反而质疑其预设的女性主义视角来思考，或由此出发，是探索为何如此的一条途径。
en: How do different understandings of the
of digital media give rise to different characterizations of the relationship

the vital and the digital? Specifically, how do various forms of medium theory adopting strong new materialist approaches respond to the message from the Silicon Valley, articulated in its products and evident in its discourse: the message about progress, about more – more technology, more activity, more agency, more control, more

? This is a message that is at odds with computational instantiations that often work to produce the opposite of all of that for the many (differentially for all of us) living within its compulsory grounds. My answer is that in so far as these accounts accept rather than question the priority of a particular sense of material advance, and therefore also precondition a response to vitalism (which is permed out from a media heuristic that is not curious about itself) they do not offer an adequate response. Thinking through, or working from, a feminist perspective that is not aligned to new materialism but rather questions its assumptions is one way to explore why not.

zh: 但这并不完全是
答案。而且，愤怒的并非只有我一人。
en: But this is not
answer entirely. And I am not the only one who is furious.

zh: 凯特·奥赖尔登、萨拉·肯伯和我出版了《愤怒》，这是一项六只手、机器辅助的技术女性主义制作，主张以其他方式思考数字唯物主义，以及它与真实、想象、象征、活力、人类和机器问题的关系。《愤怒》试图生成一种与新唯物主义总体决裂的数字唯物主义形式，尽管它同情并珍视新唯物主义某些代表人物的修复性工作。它主张，一种继续重视批判的女性主义可以指出，为何需要新取径来应对计算发展——这些发展进一步模糊了有意义的能动性形式与谁或什么可以拥有能动性、可以成为行动者之间的区分；它还主张，女性主义认识论可以提示生成这些取径的方式。与罗西·布拉伊多蒂和一种肯定式女性主义相反，我们断言这种女性主义模式仍有继续的可能，尽管我们也认识到，必须重新思考它可以如何、在何处进行，它可能处于什么情境，以及它如何被
或
en: Kate O’Riordan, Sarah Kember and I published

as a six-handed, machine-assisted, techno-feminist production, arguing for other ways to think about digital materialism and/ in its relationship to questions of the real, the imaginary, the symbolic, the vital, the human and the machine.

seeks to generate a form of digital materialism that breaks with new materialism(s) in general, even while it is sympathetic to, and values the restorative work of, some of its exponents. It argues that a feminism that continues to value critique can point to why new approaches are needed to grapple with computational developments that blur still further divisions between meaningful forms of agency and who or what may hold agency, or be an agent, and that feminist epistemologies can suggest way to generate them. Contra Rosi Braidotti and a feminism of affirmation we assert the continuing possibility of this mode of feminism, although we also recognize the necessity of rethinking how and where it might be undertaken, what its possible situation might be, and how it might be
or

zh: 在遵循《愤怒》论证的程度上，这篇文章根本不属于我。它属于我们，至少是六只手——而且所有这些手都被增强了。
en: To the extent that it follows the arguments of
, this essay is not mine at all. It is ours, a six-hander at least – and all of those hands are augmented.

zh: 那么，其他人在哪里？数字媒介艺术家黑特·史德耶尔曾在伦敦 ICA 做过一场表演讲座，核心是一颗并不在那里的子弹，尽管它不断通过手势被召唤出来。

讲座为那颗子弹留出了空间。人们感受到它幽灵般的存在——尽管它无法发射。撰写本文时，我意识到一种结构性的缺席：我缺少合著者们那有力的骨架。本文是对同样在 ICA 所作演讲的展开，部分带有回顾性质。如果我现在援引她们，不仅是为了支撑我的立场或增强我的火力，也不仅是为了引用伦理。这是因为《愤怒》试图通过一个写作过程，也通过产生一项成果，来回应关于女性主义与数字唯物主义的问题——这是它自身与再现性探究模式保持一定距离的方式之一。
en: So where are the others? The digital media artist Hito Steyerl once gave a performance lecture at the ICA in London centred on a bullet that wasn’t there, although it was constantly invoked through gesture.

A space in the talk was reserved for the bullet. Its spectral presence was felt – although it couldn’t fire. Writing this essay, an elaboration of a talk also given at the ICA, in part a retrospective, I too am aware of a structuring absence: I am missing the virtuous armature of my co-writers. If I now invoke them, this is not only with the aim of shoring up my position or amplifying my firepower; nor is it done only in the interest of citational ethics. It is because

set out to respond to questions about feminism and digital materialism(s) through a writing process, as well as by producing an output – this was one of the ways it was itself at some distance from the representational mode of inquiry.

zh: 《愤怒》通过生产一个写作之体，探索了一个数字写作之体可以
什么：于是是一种双重化的具身，它把自己定位在一个日益普遍（强制性）的媒介系统之内，却不认为自己完全由其在其中的位置所定义。
——她宣称个体声音的终结、它向网络的消散，以及写作与代码的混淆
——我们主张一个身体，一个被增强的身体，属于我们。我们的技术延伸与我们连续，但它们并未占有我们。也许最简单的说法是（我会回到这一点，因为它涉及人类与物的差异性能动性问题）：我们主张了作者身份。
en: explored what a digital writing body can

by producing a body of writing: a redoubled embodiment, then, and one that located itself within an increasingly pervasive (compulsory) media system but did not see itself as entirely defined by its place there.
Joanna Drucker, who declares the end of the individual voice, its dispersal into networks, and the confusion of writing and code,

we claimed a body, an augmented body, that was ours. Our technical extensions were continuous with us, but they did not claim us. Perhaps the simplest way to put this – and one that I will come back to since it relates to questions of differential agency, that of humans and that of things – is that we claimed authorship.

zh: 《愤怒》是一项关于作者身份的试验：不仅通过探索所创作之物（一个作品体）来理解作者身份，也通过考虑什么/谁在
：那些写作之手、那些技术义肢，以及它们与写作之手之间由技术所促成却并不对等的关系，以及其他生产、流通、分配过程。它试图成为瓦尔特·本雅明在一次对作者身份与政治意图的独特探索中所定义的“操作性的”
——其关键在于政治“倾向”与文学“倾向”之间的某种对应。《愤怒》与此相连，因为它采取的形式挤压出它所表达的希望，而在两种情况下，挤压与表达都意在
。我在此把“操作化”理解为一种物质或文学的表达，并且——现在跟随弗兰科·莫雷蒂而非本雅明，进入数字领域——意味着新概念的建构。
en: was an experiment in authorship when the latter is construed not only by exploring what is authored (a body of work) but also by considering what/who

: those writing hands, those technical prostheses and/in their afforded but non-equal relation, those other processes of production, circulation, distribution. It sought to be what Walter Benjamin, in a peculiar exploration of authorship and political intent, once defined as ‘operational’
– the key to this being a certain correspondence between a political and literary ‘tendency’.
connects to this in the sense that the form it takes extrudes the hope it expresses, and in both cases the extrusion and the expression are meant

I take operationalization here to imply a material or literary articulation and also, now following Franco Moretti rather than Benjamin, and moving onto digital terrain, to entail the construction of new concepts.

zh: 其中之一是激进的交叉性。《愤怒》以把计算资本主义置于（被误称的）人类世语境中开始并结束；人类世被视为与所有人类与非人类的未来可能性相连，并被视为本质上在与处境、位置、排斥、歧视和暴力的差异的关系中被经验。这是确认需要阐明一种交叉性模式的起点：这种交叉性始于但不停止于人类的交叉；它在探索人类与非人类之间边界的同时，打开了“人类”范畴。这借鉴但也决裂于卡伦·巴拉德新唯物主义意义上的“内行动”（intra-activity），后者是理解能动性的一种方式。它承认这样一种意图的价值：把否则可能通过话语被援引之物物质化——在人格形成的叙述中，更广泛地说，在关于能动性或在世界中行动与回应之能力的叙述中。但它反对内行动将一切开创性之物（一切要紧之物）如此彻底地奠基于不可预视
的相遇之中。说得绕口一点，一种以“内交叉”（intra-sectional）为基础的推定性政治，可以让物质本身比从前更要紧（巴拉德的要求是它应该如此）
，但随之而来的问题是，如何解释被带入交叉点的东西，那先在的经验、状况或历史。所有这些因素都有助于说明
交叉性政治被认为是必要的，为什么它的重要性继续得到证明。
en: One of these is a radical intersectionality.

begins and ends by locating computational capitalism within the contexts of the (misnamed) Anthropocene; the latter being taken as continuous with all human and non-human future possibilities, and as essentially experienced in relation to difference in situation, position, exclusion, discrimination and violence. This is the starting point for the identification of the need to elaborate a mode of intersectionality that begins with but does not stop at human crossings; that opens up the category ‘human’ even as it simultaneously explores the boundaries between human and non-human. This draws on, but also breaks with, Karen Barad’s new materialist sense of intra-activity as a way to understand the agential. It recognizes the intention of materializing what might otherwise be invoked through discourse, in accounts of the formation of personhood and more broadly in accounts of agency or the capacity to act and respond in the world as valuable. But it is at odds with the degree to which intra-activity founds all that is inaugural (all that matters) in the unprevisible
encounter. To put it tongue-twistily, a putative politics based on the intra-sectional could allow matter itself to matter more than it mattered before (Barad’s demand being that it should),
but the problem that then arises is how to account for that which is brought to the intersection, that pre-existing experience, or condition, or history. All these factors contribute to
an intersectional politics is found necessary, to why its importance continues to be demonstrated.

zh: 因此，认识到需要把交叉性重新物质化，以回应人类世所逼出的迫切要求，我们并不寻求发展一种“内交叉”叙述，而是要建立一种激进的交叉性形式。它扩展能动性，承认行动者的多样性，承认假定所有行动者（归根结底）都只是替人类行事的代理者（掌控的幻想）是徒劳的，但仍然断言（后）人类存在的独特性——作为一种活着的存在形式，它与异质活力的预设形成对照（无论这种活力是稀薄还是浓厚地分布）——并坚持具体人类行动的独特性。它使批判成为可能。
en: So, recognizing a need to re-materialize intersectionality in relation to the demands made urgent by the Anthropocene, we did not seek to develop an intra-sectional account but rather to build a radical form of intersectionality. This expands agency, recognizes a diversity of agents, acknowledges the futility of assuming all are (in the last analysis) agents of the human (the fantasy of mastery), but asserts nonetheless the distinctiveness of (post-) human being, as a form (of) being alive which stands in contradistinction to the presumption of a heterogenous vitality – whether this is spread thin or thick – and insists on the distinctiveness of specifically human actions. It enables critique.

zh: 它也允许笑声。事实上，它部分地通过笑声运作。如果《愤怒》主张建构一种激进的交叉性政治，作为对数字状况的回应，它也试图在自己的取径中把这种政治中可能重要的某些要素付诸操作。具体而言，《愤怒》援引了埃莱娜·西苏，她宣称弑神者美杜莎的笑声是一种女性主义武器，是女性主义同时肯定
批判、主张理性

瓦解一种排他性理性主张的方式——这种理性通过排除许多要紧之物（包括要紧的身体）来运作。笑声让写作得以放开喉咙、变得过度，也可能是一种拒绝/混淆/化解物质性与其意义之间所立区分的途径。它也是一种断言或探索写作与代码之间区分的方式，即便一方不断通过另一方被表达。于是，笑声是我们的操作符之一。它可以扰乱自然化的主张与预设，包括那些通常区分理性与情动、观念与物质、自然与文化的预设。此外，笑声可以促成一种论辩模式，这种模式不以深思熟虑为唯一依据（当然不至于意味着通过调制总能达成和解），同时也立足于对抗。笑声揭穿愚蠢——按照帕特里克·克罗根的定义（他尤其关心数字实现的愚蠢），愚蠢就是未能追问我们如何被治理。
en: It also allows for laughter. Indeed it in part works through it. If

advocates the construction of a radical intersectional politics as a response to the digital condition, it also sought to make operational in its own approaches some of the elements that might be important in that politics. Specifically,
invoked Hélène Cixous, who declared the laughter of the god-slayer Medusa a feminist weapon, a way for feminism to at once affirm
critique, claim rationality

undermine the exclusionary claims of a rationality that works by excluding much that matters – including bodies that matter. Laughter allows writing to become full-throated, to be excessive, and may be a means through which to refuse/confuse/defuse divisions erected between materiality and its meaning. It is also a means through which to assert or explore distinctions between writing and code, even while one is constantly articulated through the other. Laughter, then, was one of our operators. It can disturb naturalized claims and assumptions, including those that conventionally divide the rational and the affective, ideation and the material, nature and culture. Laughter moreover can enable a mode of argumentation that is predicated not on deliberation alone (certainly not to the degree that this implies an always possible reconciliation through modulation) but that also rests on antagonism. Laughter calls out stupidity – the latter defined, following Patrick Crogan, who is concerned in particular with digitally realized stupidity, as failing to ask how we are governed.

children: 笑声、新唯物主义与媒介理论

zh: 笑声具有交流性。这对我们也有用。笑声可以嘲弄地回应当代各种数字媒介唯物主义所特有的、对物质“真相”的那种完全严肃而极其激烈的关注。后一种关注错失了目标，因为它拒绝看见（也）在那里的东西，拒绝看见一切使事物变得浓厚、使之象征化、使之
的东西。我们现在不妨承认，写这本书的冲动之一，是对‘断绝交流’（excommunication，亦指‘逐出教门’）这一预告的一种愤怒；那种处境将会到来，而我们正坐在它的门槛上。与此同时，据说交流本身正陷入麻烦。亚历克斯·加洛韦对这种麻烦的叙述从解释学与内在性开始，随后被第三种模式取代——他通过召唤复仇女神（动物、“母狗”、玷污性的造物）来命名这一模式，她们定义了我们现在所处的网络复杂性状况。
针对（完全非人的）复仇女神那种恶魔般的强度，以及以她们为形象似乎会引导出的后批判回应，我们提出美杜莎的愤怒笑声。对西苏而言，笑声是
。因此，笑声可以扰乱或质疑‘断绝交流’叙述的序列（解释学、症状学、集群/系统），也可以质疑把这些序列翻译为据说由它们界定的媒介形式/格式：文本、图像、系统（机器、网络）。与加洛韦的主张相反，最后的“系统”不必，也并不总是或完全地，“组合并
”其他媒介形式。

children: Laughter, new materialism and media theory

en: Laughter communicates. This was also of use to us. Laughter can respond mockingly to the entirely serious and very fierce attention paid to the material ‘truth’ that characterizes the approach of various contemporary digital media materialisms. This latter is an attention that misses its mark because it refuses to see what is (also) there, all that which thickens, symbolizes,

. We may as well admit now that one of the spurs to writing the book was a kind of fury with the suggestion of excommunication; as that situation which will come, on whose doorstep we sit. Meanwhile, it is argued, communication itself is in trouble. Alex Galloway’s account of this trouble begins with hermeneutics and immanence, which are then superseded by a third mode, designated by his invocation of the Furies (animals, ‘bitches’, defiling creatures), who come to define that condition of networked complexity we are now in.
Against the daemonic intensity of the (entirely inhuman) Furies, and the post-critical response their figuration would seem to curate, we set the furious laughter of Medusa. For Cixous laughter is

. It may therefore disrupt or dispute the seriality of the ex-communicative account (hermeneutics, symptomatics, swarms/systems) and for that matter the translation of these to the media forms/formats they are said to define: the text, the image, the system (the machine, the network). Contra Galloway’s claim, the last ‘system’ does not have to, or does not always or entirely, ‘combine and
’ the others.

zh: 《愤怒》理解系统思维，接受网络化的状况，但不“放弃”在场或差异，也不是非人的。相反，作为一个偶然的后人类身体，愤怒地写作并怀着共同意图，我们寻求找到方式，不止通过“狂怒化”来“让世界逃离”，而且我们对对抗可能意味着什么、对“愤怒的媒介”可能得到何种回应有不同的理解。
我们在此并非完全针对复仇女神写作。加洛韦还提示了第四条路：在可憎而难以忍受的甜蜜之中的爱，代表某种超越对抗与差异的东西。我们随时都会站复仇女神一边反对这条道路，而且我们认为她们或许自有其道理。在另一个时代，西苏为女性写作提出两个目标：去“摧毁”，以及预见不可预见之物，也就是“投射”。换言之，“用笑声打破‘真相’”，然后追问什么可以重新得到肯定。
这也许还意味着，可以以较少分裂的方式探索门户之外的前景（例如更强的 AI 可能作为“异类”媒介打开什么）。也许这过于玄奥。可能需要一些阐释。
en: understands systems thinking, and accepts a networked condition, but does not ‘abdicate’ presence or difference, nor is it inhuman. On the contrary, as a contingent post-human body, writing furiously and with shared intent, we seek to find ways to do more than ‘put the world in flight’ through ‘infuriation’ and we have a different sense of what antagonism can imply, of what a response to ‘furious media’ might be.

We are not entirely writing against the Furies here. There is also the fourth way suggested by Galloway: a love in the middle of execrable, insufferable sweetness, standing for something beyond antagonism and difference. We’d back the Furies against this any day, and we think they may have their reason(s). In a different era, Cixous suggested two aims for women writing: to ‘destroy’ and to foresee the unforeseeable, which is to say to ‘project’. In other words, ‘break up the “truth” with laughter’ and then ask what may be newly affirmed.

This might also mean that the prospects of what lies beyond the portal (or what stronger AI, for instance, might open up as ‘alien’ media) could be explored in less schismatic ways. Perhaps that is gnomic. Some explication might be necessary.

zh: 让我们在此指出，断绝交流理论（姑且这样称呼）只是新媒介新唯物主义的一种变体，后者本身游弋于一片更大的海域。新唯物主义是一个标签，被赋予四五种思想脉络——思辨实在论、客体导向本体论（OOO）、作为媒介理论的数字唯物主义、新唯物主义女性主义——其中尤以巴拉德（把量子唯物主义作为后批判）
和某种程度上布拉伊多蒂（带有或多或少的德勒兹倾向）为代表。布拉伊多蒂本人正确地质疑了在这些构形中把新唯物主义称为“新”的主张，承认唯物主义传统早于当前许多形式。
毕竟，早在哈曼与 OOO、思辨实在论、软件研究以及对康德相关主义的攻击之前，女性主义就已经在思考身体与文本。另一方面，这些新唯物主义（或准新唯物主义）形式共享一种被称为“氛围”的东西
，一种对后结构主义的或多或少当代的不满，
对历史唯物主义、批判理论和“怀疑的解释学”的敌意（如凯斯顿·萨瑟兰在本卷中所指出的），这种敌意采取新的形式。
en: Let us note here that excommunication theory (to call it that) is only one variant of new media new materialism, which itself swims in a larger sea. New materialism is a label given to four or five strands of thinking – speculative realism, objected oriented ontology (OOO), digital materialism as medium theory, new materialist feminisms – those of Barad (quantum materialism as post-critique)

and to some extent Braidotti (with a more or less Deleuzean slant), notably. Braidotti herself rightly questions the claim to new materialism as ‘new’ in these formations, acknowledging traditions of materialism that pre-date many of the present forms.

Feminism, after all, was thinking about bodies as well as texts long before Harman and the OOO, speculative realism, software studies and attacks on Kantian correlationism. On the other hand, these forms of new materialism (or quasi-new materialism) share what has been called an ‘atmosphere’,
a more or less contemporary discontent with post-structuralism
a hostility to historical materialism, critical theory and the ‘hermeneutics of suspicion’ (as Keston Sutherland notes in this volume), which takes new forms.

zh: 这意味着，探索尤西·帕里卡所说的“作为媒介理论的新唯物主义”
的前景，要求承认我们正呼吸着这种“氛围”（或许可以把它定义为一个局势），也要求承认即便在媒介理论内部也存在不同变体。下文我将把关注焦点从批判理论（加洛韦）转向德国媒介理论/媒介考古学唯物主义，以追寻或重新发现活力与数字之间的联系。
en: This means that exploring what Jussi Parikka has called the prospects for ‘new materialism as media theory’

demands acknowledgement that we are breathing in this ‘atmosphere’ (perhaps this could be defined as a conjuncture), and also perhaps an acknowledgement that even within media theory there are different variants. In what follows, I shift the focus of attention from critical theory (Galloway) towards German medium theory/media archaeological materialisms in order to pursue, or to re-find, a linkage between the vital and the digital.

children: 死的还是活的？无中介的媒介？

zh: 快速绕道简·贝内特关于活力唯物主义的有影响的讨论，在此有用。贝内特在各种集合体（不区分是重点之一）中发现一种活力或能动能力，她将其作为“物之力”（thing power）来探索。在《活力物质：物的政治生态学》中，她主张“可食之物、商品、风暴和金属作为准行动者，拥有自己的轨迹、潜能和倾向”，并促成了使网络或集合体得以运作的东西。对象中固有某种力量，这种力量无法完全以人类术语理解，必须在对象自身、其物质中被发现。贝内特因此可以问：

children: Dead or alive? Media without mediation?

en: A rapid detour through Jane Bennett’s influential discussion of vital materialism is useful here. Bennett finds in assemblages of many kinds (non-differentiation is part of the point) a vitality or agential capacity that she explores as ‘thing power’. In

she argues that ‘edibles, commodities, storms and metals act as quasi agents with their own trajectories, potentialities and tendencies’ and contribute to what makes networks or assemblages operational. A force inheres in objects that is not fully comprehensible in human terms, a force that must be found in the object itself, its material. Bennett can thus ask:

zh: 什么算作活力唯物主义的物质？仅仅是人类劳动和由男人们使用原材料所制造的社会经济实体吗？还是物质性比这更有力量？政治理论如何能更好地认识非人力量在每个事件和每次稳定化中的积极参与？是否存在一种理论形式，能够承认某种“物之力”，即对象无法被化约为它们同时也体现的人类意义或议程？
en: What counts as the material of vital materialism? Is it only human  labour and the socio-economic entities made by men using raw  materials? Or is materiality more potent than that? How can political  theory do a better job of recognizing the active participation of  nonhuman forces in every event and every stabilization? Is there a  form of theory that can acknowledge a certain ‘thing-power’, that is,  the irreducibility of objects to the human meanings or agendas they  also embody?

zh: 贝内特明确表示，她更喜欢那些或许先前被视为惰性之物的更有力量的物质性，而不是由人类“事物”（例如社会经济）主导的实体；在她设想的模型中，人类（以及其他行动者）虽然保留各种能动性，但这种能动性被削弱了：当物变得有生命，人就被视为更加惰性——二者也被分开；不允许有义肢或延伸。斯科特·拉什曾指出，活力论在历史上从未过多关注人类，这一点在此也很明显。这或许部分解释了为什么“男人们”（原文如此）所制造的东西在贝内特的叙述中显得格格不入，因为它当然依赖一种活力论模式。正是这种模式提供了能动性形式，提供了一种有时似乎充满
（élan vital）的潜能。贝内特在多个事物及其集合体中发现的潜能带有神秘主义色彩。这些集合体如何被装配则不太清楚；如果它们交流，它们当然并不
en: Bennett is clear that she prefers the more potent materialities of what might have previously been thought inert over entities dominated by human ‘things’ (socio-economics, for instance), and while humans (among other actants) retain forms of agency in the models she envisages this is reduced: as things become live humans are viewed as more inert – they are also kept apart; no prosthesis or extension is allowed. Scott Lash has noted that vitalism has historically never been much preoccupied with the human, and this is evident here too. It may be partly why what is made by ‘men’ (
) sits uneasily in Bennett’s account since it certainly relies on a mode of vitalism. It is that which provides for forms of agency, for a potency that sometimes appears charged with an

There are mystical undertones to the potentialities Bennett finds in multiple things and in their assemblages. How the latter are assembled is less clear, and if they communicate they certainly do not

zh: 对新媒介的新唯物主义分析也关心理解物质力量，也面对这一力量如何有活力、如何运作的问题（并在一种被投注的关系中处理该问题：技术投入到认知自动化，而此事关联能动性与活性），但它们在不同的边界集合上运作。这一次，任务不是模糊区分无生命物（及其能动性）与有意识存在的边界。相反，同样是为了（一种新的）唯物主义，另一组相当不同的边界将被恢复。
en: New materialist analyses of new media, also concerned to understand material force and also confronting the question of how that force is lively, or how it operates (and doing so in relation to that cathected relationship between a technology invested in the automation of cognition and matters of agency, and liveliness), operate at a different set of borders. This time the task is not to blur boundaries dividing inanimate things (and their agency) from conscious beings. Rather, but also in the interests of a (new) materialism, a rather different set of boundaries are to be reinstated.

zh: 关键在于把媒介与介质、真实与再现分开。贝内特倾听，听到某种类似生命力的东西。新媒介唯物主义优先剥除附着在数字材料或数字操作之上的种种归因，犹如刮去藤壶（包括贝内特的神秘硬壳），以便更仔细地审视真实之物。贝内特想把一个物从人们认定的惰性中撬出来，寻求理解其活性与能动性的方式；作为媒介理论的新唯物主义则相反，致力于把媒介物从其历史语境、视域中撬出，并在这样做时剥去它的附着物、它的
，后者被认为不健康。技术媒介对象与系统而非再现。描述那里有什么，而不是可能把它包覆起来的理论化。

你或许可以说，数字媒介理论中的物质转向产生了一种坚持：寻找物的本质。其余之物被认为非本质，是一层可被蜕去的外皮，是我们本可不要的果皮，或一种我们必须克服的过滤习惯；这种习惯就是相信魔法（贝内特的作品因这一点而遭拒斥），或相信中介——后一种习惯接受世界按照我们能够感知它的方式、按照我们使之有意义的方式来到我们面前。这条路线将产生对技术媒介及其（真实）力量的理解；那种力量先于意义问题而存在和运作，无论这些意义问题可能如何被解释和评估。
en: The point is to divide media from medium, the real from the representational. Bennett listens in and hears something like a life force. New media materialism makes it a priority to strip away the barnacles of what is imputed to digital materials or to digital operations (including Bennett’s mystic encrustations) in order to look harder at the real thing. Where Bennett wants to winkle a thing out of its perceived inertia, seeking ways to understand its aliveness and its agency, new materialism as a medium theory works instead to winkle the media thing out of its historical contexts, its horizons, and in doing so to strip it of its accretions, its
, which are regarded as unhealthy. Technical media objects and systems not representations. Description of what is there, not theorizations that might encrust it.

You might say the material turn in digital medium theory produces an insistence on finding the essence of the thing. The rest is thought inessential, an outer skin to be sloughed off, a rind we could do without or a filter habit we need to get over; the habit being to believe in magic (Bennett’s work has been rejected for this) or in mediation, the latter being a habit of accepting that the world comes to us as we are able to sense it and as we make it meaningful. This is the route that will produce an understanding both of technical media and of its (real) power; that which stands and operates prior to matters of significance as these might be interpreted and assessed.

zh: 在基特勒著作所体现、后来经沃尔夫冈·恩斯特关于时间性的研究发展的那支德国媒介理论中（二者属于同一传统，后者也被界定为一种媒介考古学），这些论证得到充分表达。它们既产生一种诊断（如基特勒所说：代码今天“决定”我们）
，也产生一种要求。这要求针对媒介形式研究采取特定分析或取径。对恩斯特和基特勒而言，这既是对发展的回应——因为技术媒介的兴起使这种探究取向变得必要，如果说此前并非如此——也构成一种迟来的承认：技术媒介或许一直都需要被如此探究。尤西·帕里卡大致在同一传统中写作，他进一步推进这一主张，并给予它本体论辩护，主张“新唯物主义已经存在于技术媒介传输和处理‘文化’的方式之中”。这一主张表述得有些古怪
，但它有用地表明：基特勒和恩斯特围绕非常具体的技术媒介所发展的取径，已经扩展到成为一系列受新唯物主义启发的计算研究中的普遍取向。它也指向（或解释了）新媒介唯物主义者为何把自己视为
——他们的分析内在于他们研究的材料。这产生了一系列肯定性的、“非意识形态的”叙述，它们凭自己的位置而自认为格外
en: In that strand of German Medium Theory embodied in Kittler’s work and latterly developed through Wolfgang Ernst’s work on temporality, which is in the same tradition and which has come also to be defined as a form of media archaeology, these arguments find full expression. They produce both a diagnosis (as Kittler put it: codes ‘determine’ us today)

and a demand. The demand is for a particular form of analysis or approach to the study of mediatic forms. For both Ernst and Kittler this is at once a response to developments, since the rise of technical media makes such investigative orientations necessary, if they were not before, and constitutes an overdue recognition of what might have always been necessary to investigate technical media. Jussi Parikka, writing in more or less the same tradition, pushes this claim further and gives it an ontological justification when he argues that ‘new materialism is already present in the way technical media transmits and processes ‘‘culture”.’ This claim is somewhat peculiarly expressed,

but it usefully indicates the degree to which approaches developed by Kittler and Ernst, around very specific technical media, have broadened to become a general orientation extant across a range of new-materialism-inspired forms of investigation of the computational. It also points to the degree to which (or why) new media materialists regard themselves as

– their analyses being immanent to the material they are studying. This produces a series of accounts that are affirmative, ‘non-ideological’, and that regard themselves by virtue of their position as exceptionally

zh: 值得注意的是，在这些取径中，要抵达的核心内核、要探索的本质性物质，被分别确定为软件、硬件、代码、算法。于是，蜕去其他一切、清除肮脏的实在（例如所有那些肮脏现实主义）
的过程，产生的不是一个，而是若干个物。那个本质并不像表面看起来那样容易把握。无论如何，我们有权再次追问：这些是什么种类的媒介对象？
en: It is striking that in these approaches the central kernel to be reached, or the essential matter to be explored, is variously determined as software, hardware, code, algorithm. The process of sloughing off of everything else, purging it of the dirty real (all that dirty realism, for instance)
thus produces not one, but a number of things. That essence is not as easy to get hold of as it might appear to be. We are at any rate entitled to ask again what kind of media objects are these?

zh: 为它们提出的主张很宏大。它们常常是庞大的对象：大数据、强大的算法、全球网络。它们的规模与触及范围也因附于其上的期票而扩展——它们似乎表述甚至物质化这些期票。
大数据指向更大数据的到来，甚至指向完整数据和一切解释必要性的终结：“所有数字”，意味着“不再需要理论”。并非偶然，克里斯·安德森这一如今臭名昭著的主张最初是在《连线》杂志获得推力的。
或者想想算法及其证明力，或关于机器学习和涌现的主张。这些例子表明这些东西如何膨胀；它们有变成不真实对象的危险，如凯特·奥赖尔登会说的那样。
但也有收缩。更仔细地看，这些东西变得越来越不实质；它们收缩。它们几乎变成想象性的；之所以说是想象性的，是因为想象性——它是这些技术物之构成的固有部分，如果这些技术物要运作的话——已被从它们之中剥离。此处关键是抽象，而不是过程；然而，这种辨识出对象、使对象从中物质化的操作/取向，却被声称触及事物的核心，触及使事物有生机的东西。这构成一种拜物教。
en: The claims made for them are big. They are often big objects: big data, powerful algorithms, global networks. Their scale and reach are also expanded by way of the promissory notes attached to them, which they seem to articulate or even materialize.

Big data points to the coming of even bigger data, and even towards complete data and the end of all necessity for interpretation: ‘all the numbers’, meaning ‘no more theory’. Un-accidentally this now notorious suggestion from Chris Anderson first gained traction in
magazine.

Or consider the algorithm, and its proving power, or claims made for machine learning and emergence. These examples point to the degree to which these things bloat; they threaten to become unreal objects, as Kate O’Riordan would put it.

But there is also shrinkage. Look harder and these things become increasingly less substantial; they shrink. They become almost imaginary; imaginary because the imaginary, which is an intrinsic part of the constitution of these technical things, if these technical things are to work, has been stripped out of them. Abstraction not process is key here, and yet this operation/ orientation through which an object is discerned, out of which it is materialized, is claimed to get to the heart of things, to get at that which animates things. This constitutes a form of fetishism.

zh: 回到经典的论述
，同时质疑它组织我们欲望的主张
覆盖着
。在试图蒸馏物本身时，物本身被根本性地削减，它与世界的关系以及其物质吸引力的
都随之黯淡。取代后者的，奇怪得很，可能是魔法性的东西。拜物教或许把一种活力论模式重新请了进来，因为传统上隐藏之物可能具有未被承认的力量。这种拜物教如何运作？这是一种媒介拜物教吗？温迪·春等人曾指出软件与代码研究中对代码的拜物教化，但这个版本可能更为彻底。
en: To refer to the classical invocation,
while disputing its claims to organize our desire,
covers a
. In attempting to distil the thing itself, the thing itself is radically diminished, and its relation to the world and the

of its material appeal are dimmed. In place of the latter, what returns might oddly enough be the magical. The fetish perhaps invites a mode of vitalism back in, since traditionally what is hidden may have unacknowledged powers. How does this fetish work? Is this a medium fetish? Wendy Chun and others have pointed to the fetishization of code within software and code studies, but this version might be more thoroughgoing.

zh: 拜物教建立在未被承认、或被遮盖（被否认）的匮乏之上。对物质的执着、对“物质”的拜物教化，使数字唯物主义得以宣称它把握了实在，而其他叙述缺乏实质或现实。它们的指控不是其他技术媒介叙述缺少对媒介权力的承认（尽管这是恩斯特等人论证的一部分）。要点在于，技术媒介最必要的维度——确实是唯一真正必要的维度——缺失了；物质地被给予的技术能力，据说在依赖二阶再现（处理死的模拟或反射）的叙述中被熨平进话语或再现，甚至被拉成一条直线。其后果（据称）是能动性的分配被误解：过多给了人类，过少给了技术系统的决定性操作——这些操作与其说中介，不如说安排秩序。
en: The fetish is based on lack that is not recognized, or that is covered over (disavowed). An adherence to the material, a fetishization of ‘the material’, allows digital materialism to say that it grasps the real while other accounts lack substance or reality. Their charge is not that what is missing in other accounts of technical media is a recognition of media power (though that is part of the argument made by Ernst, for example). The point is that the most necessary dimension, indeed the only really necessary dimension of technical media, is missing; that materially given technical capacity, which is said to be ironed out into discourse or representation, flatlined even, in accounts relying on second-order representations (dealing in dead simulation or reflection). A consequence of this (it is argued) is that the allocation of agency is misunderstood; too much being given to humans, and too little to the determining operations of technical systems – which do not so much mediate as order.

zh: 思考媒介拜物教化，或许是一种解释媒介理论敌意的途径，这种敌意针对关于新媒介的其他叙述，因为它们纠缠于其他形式的拜物教化（以及异化与误认）：马克思关于商品关系的叙述——人与人的关系被误认为物与物的关系——以及弗洛伊德的叙述——欲望被误认，产生一种自我异化形式。
en: Thinking about medium fetishization might be a way to account for the hostility found in medium theory towards other accounts of new media that tangle with other forms of fetishization (and with alienation and misrecognition): Marx’s account of commodity relations, in which relations between people are mistaken for relations between things, and Freud’s, in which desire is misrecognized, producing a form of self-alienation.

zh: 总体而言，新唯物主义会把这类构形当作（几乎字面意义上）没有实质的东西加以清扫，认为它们以错误的方式看错误的东西（或许只是向后看）。
en: In general, new materialism would sweep away such formations as (almost literally) without substance, as looking in the wrong way, at the wrong thing (perhaps as simply looking backwards).

zh: 然而，通过拜物教的视角探索新唯物主义媒介理论，提供了一种方式，可借此勾勒新唯物主义数字媒介叙述中的缺失。在这些叙述中，商品关系问题与欲望之事以其缺席而在场，是拜物教化叙述所遮盖——无法处理——之物的一部分；这或许也解释了它为何不能或不愿从生理性别与社会性别的区分出发思考，也看不到为何对性别的系统叙述必然与同一系统的其他要素相交织（即便对处理歧视有明显同情的取向，例如帕里卡的情形）。今天，马克思在社会关系中看到的误认（人与人的关系被误认为物与物的关系），他也始终理解为作用于身体（并促成对身体的伤害）的误认，现在作用于那些被分割化、由数据生产、被要求自行担责、在很大程度上被剥夺能动性并遭受歧视的信息主体的身体；作用于一般社会关系以及我们每个人的生活。取道拜物教并非唯一路径。我们自己当然不会把它“在理论上”所采取的两种经典形式简单并列。
但若以为可以绕过这些实例化关系、物质复杂性与缠结、这些构形所指向的想象，仍然生产或找到数字对象的核或“真相”，那确实可笑。
en: However, exploring new materialist media theory through the perspective of the fetish provides a means through which to adumbrate what is missing in new materialist accounts of digital media. In them, the question of commodity relations and the matter of desire are present in their absence, are part of what the fetishized account covers up – cannot deal with – which may also be why it cannot or does not wish to think in terms of sex–gender distinctions, and also does not see why a systematic account of gender necessarily intersects with other elements of the same system (this being so even when a sympathetic orientation towards tackling discrimination is evident, as for example is the case for Parikka). Today a version of that misrecognition that Marx saw in social relations (where relations between people are mistaken for relations between things), which he also always understood to operate on bodies (to contribute to harming them), now operates on the bodies of the dividuated, data-produced, responsibilized, largely de-agentialized and discriminated subjects of information; operates on the social relation in general and on each of our lives. Going by way of the fetish is not the only way to go. We ourselves certainly would not parallel the two canonical forms it has taken ‘in theory’.

But it is laughable indeed to consider that it is possible to reach around the instantiated relations, the material complexities and imbrications, the imaginaries these formations point to, and still produce or find the kernel or the ‘truth’ of the digital object.

zh: 在其一些挑衅性的后政治脉络中，新唯物主义媒介分析实际上并不（太）关心这些事情，而更关心完全超出人类的问题。在这个意义上，或在这个变体中，它是反人类的。或者它可能关心，但预设这类问题只能通过被视为“先在”之物（恩斯特）或结构决定之物（德鲁克）的途径来接近。从它自身的术语看，对新媒介唯物主义更严厉的指控——它当然会试图反驳——或许是：它对实在的主张，因未能把握它试图接触的那些材料的全部维度而受损。一种说法是：它无法对它发现自己身处其中的构形产生回应（批判性的或其他），相反（仅仅）与它连续。
en: In some of its defiantly post-political veins, new materialist media analysis doesn’t actually care (much) about these things, being more interested in issues beyond the human entirely. It is in this sense, or in this variant, anti-human. Or it may care but presume such issues may not be approached except by way of what is viewed as ‘prior’ (Ernst), or structurally determining (Drucker). Seen in its own terms, the graver charge against new media materialism, which it would of course seek to refute, might be that its claims to the real are undermined by a failure to grasp the full dimensions of those materials it is seeking to engage with. One way to put this is to suggest that it cannot generate a response (critical or otherwise) to the formation it finds itself in but is on the contrary (simply) continuous with it.

children: “因此，为了抵抗当下，我提议”，或者，一条金鱼回应

zh: 为了把这与活力和生命重新联系起来，我想迅速从理论跳到一条金鱼。更确切地说，跳到马修·温斯坦的动画视频《E Lobro》
，其中心是一条被女性化的金鱼蜿蜒游动——它同时嘲弄生命与人类性别区分，又演绎这些区分，在像金鱼缸中植物一样细长而过度生长的骨架之间滑行。
温斯坦的鱼和他的骨架一样死气沉沉，而我们无限确信它们都不曾真正活过，尽管全都高度动画化。这里的美学或许与克莱尔·科尔布鲁克所说的酷儿活力论相共鸣——作为潜能场域的被动活力论，它将使生命（包括性别化生命）得以实现——但也可能是其反面：处理一种死的潜能。
早期人工生命探索往往通过诡异感来运作，把这种感觉建立在“生命出现在不应出现之处”的感觉上（《大都会》再次可能是典型例子）。然而在此，这种诡异感已被驱散。我们或许只剩下罗莎琳德·高尔特所探讨的漂亮或装饰性。

children: ‘Thus, to resist the present, I propose’, or, a goldfish responds

en: In the interests of linking this back to vitality and life, I want to rapidly jump from theory to a goldfish. More precisely to Matthew Weinstein’s animated video

at the centre of which are the sinuous perambulations of a feminized goldfish – at once mocking life and human gender divisions and enacting them, as it slides between skeletons that are spindly and overgrown like the plants in a goldfish bowl.

Weinstein’s fish is just as dead as his skeletons, and we are endlessly sure that none of them has ever quite lived, although all are highly animated. The aesthetic here might seem to resonate with what Claire Colebrook has described as a queer vitalism – passive vitalism as a field of potentialities that would enable life (including gendered life) to actualize – but might also be its obverse: dealing in a dead potentiality.
Early explorations of artificial life tended to work through the uncanny, founding this on that sense of life found where it should not be (
, again, might be a canonical example). Here though, that has been routed. We are left, perhaps, with what Rosalind Galt has explored as the pretty or the decorative.

zh: 温斯坦的作品既演绎数字的拜物教（作为媒介拜物教），又对它作出评论。这样做时，它找到了一种

在线、被建构、屏幕上的身体状况的方式。这件作品当然不是教育性的，也不完全是抵抗性的，但它具有诊断性，并揭示某种特定的可感者分配目前如何被操作、如何施展吸引力。相比之下，硬媒介唯物主义无视想象，无法处理它所演绎的拜物教，因而太容易（并非必然）不去追问工业所提供的未来图景，而是径直漂入与它的结盟。新媒介唯物主义更奇怪的一点是，它在坚持物质的同时，最终追随了行业炒作。或许我们可以说，它被现存的不真实对象晃花了眼。
en: Weinstein’s work both enacts the fetish of the digital, as medium fetish, and comments on it. In doing so a way is found to look

at the online, constructed, on-screen bodily condition. This work is certainly not pedagogic and nor is it resistive exactly, but it is diagnostic and revelatory of ways in which a particular distribution of the sensible is currently operated and makes its appeal. By contrast, disregarding the imaginary, unable to deal with the fetish it enacts, hard medium materialism all too easily (not inevitably) does not interrogate, but simply drifts into alignment with, that vision of the future offered by industry. One of the odder things about new media materialism is the extent to which, insisting on the material, it is in the end following the industry hype. Perhaps we might say it is dazzled by extant unreal objects.

zh: 同样对斜视感兴趣的《愤怒》，作为一个从事写作的身体和一个写作成果之体，构成对新媒介唯物主义的另一种不完全属于人类的回应——后者被当作思考新媒介的规范视角。顺便说，这也是一个我们并不加以拜物化的身体。我们站在它背后，我、我、我，承认我们行动的限制和我们的可问责性，却并未由此呈现出一种缺席。正是通过一种既被主张又被部分拒绝（或被化解，以使它的权威质疑自身）的作者身份——它与实现明显不同，但与它共享一种肯定感——我们找到行动的空间，同时也承认我们的位置与场所。要点是找到一个写作的位置：既不是从不可能的“外部”（无中介的幻想可能把我们置于那里），也不是完全从内部得到确保——像新唯物主义媒介理论那样，相信自己在本体论上被决定的方式，恰与它所研究的材料相同。针对物质的拜物教——它产生一种匮乏的叙述，却坚持其肯定性，并坚持它完全真实——《愤怒》的回应是坚持写作的具体物质性（包括其中的自动化，以及它对手工劳动的要求），也坚持数字的物质性。它坚持二者的相互依赖。
en: Also interested in looking askance,

, as a writing body and as a body of writing, constitutes another kind of not entirely human response to new media materialism as a normative perspective for thinking about new media. It is also, by the way, a body we do not fetishize. We stand behind it, I and I and I, recognizing our limits of movement, and our accountability, but not registering an absence. It is by way of an authorship at once asserted and partially refused (or defused so that its authority questions itself), which is conspicuously different from an actualization, but which shares with it a sense of affirmation, that we find room to move while also recognizing our place and location. The point was to find a place to write neither from the impossible outside, where the fantasy of un-mediation might place us, nor as entirely secured from within – as a new materialist medium theory that takes its status as ontologically determined in precisely the same way as the materials it studies believes itself to be. Against the fetish of the material which produces an account that is lacking while insisting it is affirmative – and insists it is entirely true –

responds by insisting on the specific materiality of writing (including in this its automation, as well as the labour it demands by hand) as well as the materiality of the digital. It insists on their co-dependence.

zh: 我们肯定数字媒介以及数字中介的身体与世界的开放潜能。我们抵抗强制/强制性之物，并非在于反对技术，更非反对信息技术。我们感兴趣的恰恰是它如何可能裂解（而非确认）一系列区分，包括活动形式与能动性形式之间的区分，以及那些以人类术语/等级来组织生命的区分。但我们保持我们的（后）人类性，并承认我们在计算资本主义中的处境位置——计算资本主义也是一个系统，却不同于纯信息论或控制论叙述所导出的系统；在后一种系统中，反馈并不理会意图，包括制造、开创、创作的意图。
en: We affirm the open potential of digital media and of digitally mediated bodies and worlds. Our resistance to compulsion/the compulsory is not located in relation to technology, let alone information technology. We are interested in precisely how it may fracture (rather than confirm) a series of divisions, including those between forms of activity and agency, and those that organize life in human terms/hierarchies. But we maintain our (post-) humanity and recognize our situated position in computational capitalism – also a system, but not that derived from an entirely informational or cybernetic account – in which feedback is indifferent to intent, including intent to make, inaugurate, author.

zh: 这也为重新思考活力论、数字与唯物主义之间的政治关系指明了道路，至少作为一种建议，开启了以超越以下二分的方式重新思考能动性的可能：活力论（作为一种非人生命力）与被限制在过于频繁地被规范性刻写的身体中的生命。这项任务或许要求重新思考数字理论中一个“传统”的特殊限制；在唐娜·哈拉维（或她的赛博格）成为赛博文化理论奠基人物的程度上，这一限制甚至被奉为神圣。它就是那个说法：“当机器变得更有活力，我们变得更加惰性。”但为什么这个总和必然成立？系统（不必）是封闭的。活动无处不在。寻找计算它的新方式，并作为女性主义技术科学中一项亲技术计划的一部分来做这件事，是一项紧迫任务。如西苏所说：“一分钟也不能耽误。我们离开这里。”
en: This also points the way for a rethinking of that political relationship between vitalism, the digital and materialism by opening – as a suggestion at least – the possibility of rethinking agency in terms that go beyond a division between vitalism (as an inhuman life force) and life as confined to the all too often normatively inscribed body. This task might entail a rethinking of a peculiar limitation that is ‘traditional’ in digital theory: to the extent that Donna Haraway (or her cyborg) has become a founding figure of cybercultural theory, it is even hallowed. It is the one that says, ‘as machines become more lively, we become more inert’. But why should this sum add up? The system (does not need to be) closed. There is activity all around. Finding new ways to calculate it and doing so as part of a technophile project of feminist technoscience is an urgent task. As Cixous put it: ‘Not a minute to lose. Let’s get out of here.’
